Need assess each requirement against claims. Need preserve IDs. We have Original Question, skeleton requirements R1-R6, verified claims C1,C2.

We must not use outside knowledge. Need determine support statuses. Let's parse.

Original Question asks: Every year teams... final prestigious programming contest. In one particular year, team featuring Australian coder won championship. Coder track record bronze, silver, gold, another silver in four consecutive IOIs. Other two teammates from same country. Tell year associated with competition title and host university for year he won that title.

Task Skeleton:
R1 Annual university programming final (source: Every year teams of competitive programmers from universities around world compete in final of prestigious programming contest for title.)
R2 Winning team and Australian coder (In one particular year, discovered team featuring Australian coder won championship.)
R3 Coder medal sequence (bronze, silver, gold, another silver in four consecutive IOIs)
R4 Other teammates country relation (His other two teammates were from same country.)
R5 Requested winning year (year associated with competition title)
R6 Requested host university (name of host university for year he won that title?)

Verified Claims:
C1: Jerry Mao is Australian competitive programmer with medals IOI 2015 bronze, 2016 silver, 2017 gold, 2018 silver. This supports R3 fully? R3 says "This coder has ... secured bronze, silver, gold, and another silver in four consecutive IOIs." C1 says exactly Jerry Mao medals 2015 bronze, 2016 silver, 2017 gold, 2018 silver. These are four consecutive IOIs? Years 2015-2018 consecutive. Yes. So R3 fully supported by C1. Also possibly identifies coder Australian for R2.

C2: Jerry Mao was member of MIT team MIT ZEROONE (with Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao), which won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022) as World Champion.
This supports R2: Winning team and Australian coder: team featuring Australian coder (Jerry Mao) won championship. C2 says Jerry Mao member of MIT team won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka as World Champion. Yes. It establishes team featuring Australian coder won championship? C2 doesn't explicitly say Jerry Mao is Australian, but C1 does. Combined C1 + C2. So R2 fully supported.

R4: His other two teammates were from same country. C2 says teammates Mingyang Deng and Xiao Mao. Does it say they are from same country? No. It names them, but no country. Could infer from MIT? No. Same country as him? Not stated. No support. C1 no. So unsupported (supported_by empty).

R1: Annual university programming final. C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka, MIT team won. Does it establish annual? No, but "ICPC World Finals" is a programming contest final? It says teams from universities? MIT team. It won World Champion. But requirement R1: "Every year, teams of competitive programmers from universities around the world compete in the final of a prestigious programming contest for the prestigious title." This is a general background claim. C2 establishes a specific instance: ICPC 2021 World Finals, MIT team. It doesn't establish that every year, teams from universities around world compete. But maybe C2 contributes to the event existence and final? The requirement is broad annual contest. Need assess material parts: annual, teams of competitive programmers from universities around world, compete in final, prestigious programming contest, title. C2 supports specific contest final and world champion, team from MIT. But not "every year", not "universities around world" (only MIT). It does establish a team from a university won a final of a programming contest. Partial support? The requirement is a general statement. C2 provides an instance of a university team competing in/wining ICPC World Finals. It substantiates "teams ... from universities ... compete in final of programming contest" for at least one contest/year. But not "Every year" nor "around the world" nor "prestigious title" maybe "World Champion" implies prestigious? Could count. So partially_supported? Need decide.

R5: Requested winning year. C2 says "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022) as World Champion." The question asks "year associated with the competition title" for the year he won that title. C2 gives ICPC 2021 World Finals, held 2022. What is associated year? Could be 2021 (competition title) or 2022 (held). The claim provides both. Does it establish the requested winning year? It says won ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka, held on 10 Nov 2022. The "year associated with competition title" likely 2021? The answer likely 2021? But we only judge support. C2 states team won ICPC 2021 World Finals. That establishes a year (2021) associated with the competition title. It also gives held date 2022. So R5 is fully supported? We need be careful: R5 requirement: "Could you tell me the year associated with the competition title" This is an information request, not a proposition? In task skeleton, requirements are what question requires to be established. For a question asking for year, support if claims provide the year. C2 provides "ICPC 2021 World Finals" and held on 10 November 2022. It gives year 2021 associated with title. So yes fully supported by C2. But if ambiguity between 2021 and 2022? The claim explicitly labels ICPC 2021 World Finals. The competition title won is "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka" so year associated is 2021. So fully supported.

R6: Requested host university. C2 says held on 10 November 2022 in Dhaka? Wait "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held on 10 November 2022)" This says location Dhaka, not host university. The question asks host university for the year he won that title. ICPC World Finals host university? In ICPC, host university? C2 mentions MIT team, not host university. It says "Dhaka" maybe host city, not university. Does it say host university? No. Could "MIT ZEROONE" team's university? No, MIT is contestant, not host. The host university for ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka? The host was University of Dhaka? Not in claims. C2 only says Dhaka, held date. No host university. So R6 unsupported. If "host university" maybe the university hosting the contest? Not provided. C2's "Massachusetts Institute of Technology team" is not host. So unsupported.

Need consider R1 again. Could be fully_supported? C2 establishes "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka" as a final of a programming contest, MIT team won as World Champion. It doesn't establish annual or universities around world. But the skeleton R1 is not just background; it's a requirement. The verified claims may not establish annual nature. Since C2 only one instance. So partial.

Need produce JSON with requirements array exactly six. For each status and supported_by. For unsupported empty. For partial, include claims. For fully, include claims.

Let's map:
R1 partially_supported supported_by ["C2"]? Maybe C2 supports "teams of competitive programmers from universities ... compete in final of a prestigious programming contest for title" because MIT team, World Finals, World Champion. It doesn't support "Every year" or "around the world". So partial.
R2 fully_supported supported_by ["C1","C2"] (C1 establishes Australian coder, C2 establishes he was team member won championship).
R3 fully_supported supported_by ["C1"].
R4 unsupported supported_by [].
R5 fully_supported supported_by ["C2"]? C2 gives ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka (held 10 Nov 2022). The question asks "year associated with the competition title" and "host university for the year he won that title." The claim gives competition title year 2021. So yes.
R6 unsupported supported_by [].

Need ensure no extra text. JSON only. Use exact schema. 

Let's think if R1 could be fully_supported because C2 "ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka" is a final of "prestigious programming contest"; but "Every year, teams ... from universities around the world compete in the final" is general. C2 doesn't support "every year" nor "around the world." So partial.

Could R2 require "In one particular year" and "won championship." C2 gives won championship in 2021/2022. Yes. Also "team featuring an Australian coder" C1 identifies Australian coder, C2 identifies team. Fully.

Could R5 require "year associated with competition title" and "year he won that title" maybe the coder won title as part of team in ICPC 2021? C2 says ICPC 2021 World Finals Dhaka. Yes.

Could R6: "name of the host university for the year he won that title" C2 mentions "Massachusetts Institute of Technology" but that's team's university, not host university. So unsupported.
